:::{#thm-sigma-algebra-closure}
#### Closure properties of a $\sigma$-algebra

If $\salg$ is a [$\sigma$-algebra](#def-sigma-algebra) on a set $S$,
then $\salg$ contains:

- the [empty set](sets-functions.qmd#def-empty-set) $\emptyset$;
- the union $A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_n$ of any [finitely many](sets-functions.qmd#def-finite-set) sets $\dsn{A}$ in $\salg$;
- the intersection $\bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i$ of any sequence $A_1, A_2, \ldots$ of sets in $\salg$.

So $\salg$ is [closed under](#def-closed-under) finite unions
and under intersections of sequences of its sets.

:::

::: proof

*Empty set.*
$\salg$ contains $S$,
so it contains the complement of $S$,
which is $S \setminus S = \emptyset$.

*Finite unions.*
Extend $\dsn{A}$ to a sequence
by setting

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{n+1} &= A_{n+2} \\
&= \cdots \\
&= \emptyset;
\end{aligned}
$$

each of these sets is in $\salg$, by the first part.
Then:

$$
\ba
A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_n
&= A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_n \cup \emptyset \cup \emptyset \cup \cdots
&& \text{(a union with } \emptyset \text{ adds no elements)} \\
&= \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i
&& \text{(} A_i = \emptyset \text{ for } i > n \text{)}
\ea
$$

and $\salg$ contains $\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i$ by the union rule of @def-sigma-algebra.

*Countable intersections.*
Each $A_i$ is a subset of $S$,
so an element of $S$ is outside $S \setminus A_i$ exactly when it is in $A_i$;
that is, $S \setminus (S \setminus A_i) = A_i$.
So, by [De Morgan's laws](sets-functions.qmd#thm-de-morgan):

$$
\ba
S \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} (S \setminus A_i)
&= \bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} \paren{S \setminus (S \setminus A_i)}
&& \text{(De Morgan's laws)} \\
&= \bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i
&& \text{(} S \setminus (S \setminus A_i) = A_i \text{)}
\ea
$$

Each $S \setminus A_i$ is in $\salg$ by the complement rule,
so their union is in $\salg$ by the union rule,
and the complement of that union is in $\salg$ by the complement rule again.

:::
